items.question: In what three syllabic forms is the vidyā beginning with kāma, vāgbhava, and tārā constituted?
premises: The vidyā is characterized as beginning with kāma, vāgbhava, and tārā.
One form of this vidyā is described as seven-syllabled.
Another form of this vidyā is described as eight-syllabled.
The vidyā is presented as existing in three ways.
items.inference: The supreme vidyā beginning with kāma, vāgbhava, and tārā is constituted in three forms, including seven-syllabled and eight-syllabled variants.
uncertainties: The exact syllabic composition of the third form is not explicitly specified in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The vidyā that begins with kāma, vāgbhava, and tārā exists in three forms: one of seven syllables, one of eight syllables, and a third form.
